claims.explanation: AM-92016 is a potassium channel blocker that may selectively kill cancer cells with high expression of potassium channels or related transporters, leading to altered membrane potential and apoptosis. The pattern of sensitive lines suggests that mutations in TP53, PTEN, and CDKN2A, which impair DNA damage and cell cycle checkpoints, may sensitize cells to the drug's effects. Additionally, the transcriptional similarity to GABA and calcium channel blockers hints at a role for calcium signaling, with high expression of calcium channels or GABA receptors potentially mediating sensitivity.

features.basis: observed pattern: many sensitive lines have TP53 mutations
observed pattern: sensitive lines include PTEN-mutant FTC238, H4, TE4, SNU81
observed pattern: sensitive lines include CDKN2A-mutant NCIH1915, LXF289, VMCUB1, RPMI7951, HEP3B217
mechanism: potassium channel blocker may target cells with high hERG expression
mechanism: delayed rectifier potassium channel blockade may affect cells with high expression
annotated target: GRIN1 is a known target of AM-92016
virtual cell similarity to mibefradil (T-type calcium channel blocker)
virtual cell similarity to saclofen (GABA receptor antagonist)
virtual cell similarity to LY225910 (CCK receptor antagonist)
virtual cell similarity to RS-17053 (adrenergic receptor antagonist)
virtual cell similarity to doxepin (histamine receptor antagonist)
observed pattern: many resistant lines have NF1 mutations
